findings.evidence: features/008-optimize-skill/008-optimize-skill-prd.md:R7 + R8 + R13 + R14 — Four mechanisms interact at runtime in ways the PRD has not traced through: (1) R7's per-target weekly budget cap (default $10/target/week, refresh at week boundary); (2) R8's branch-per-run with declined branches retained ≥30 days; (3) R13's 30-day target skip after 3 consecutive declines; (4) R14's single open PR per target enforced at pre-flight. The interaction the PRD does not specify: when a target is in the 30-day-skip state (R13) AND the maintainer manually invokes `/optimize {target}` with a manually-tightened eval to break the decline streak, does the manual invocation override the 30-day skip, refuse, or warn-and-proceed? R13's chat-line warning fires 'when the maintainer next invokes `/optimize` manually,' which suggests the manual invocation is allowed to proceed — but the cron-skip mechanism reads the same record. If the manual run lands a `merged` decision, does the cron resume targeting the skill on the next nightly run, or wait the remaining 30-day-skip window? Conversely: when a 'closed-without-merge' branch from 25 days ago is still open as a stale branch (R8 retention), AND a fresh manual invocation runs on the same target, R14's single-open-PR check is satisfied (no open PR — the PR is closed) BUT the stale branch exists. Does the new run's branch name collide? R8 disambiguates with timestamps but the cleanup mechanism (housekeeping skill) is deferred. A maintainer running `/optimize {target}` weekly would accumulate stale branches indefinitely.
findings.claim: Cross-artefact ambiguity (interaction-mode coverage gap) — the four runtime mechanisms (R7 budget refresh, R8 branch retention, R13 30-day skip + manual override, R14 single-open-PR) have unspecified interaction modes for the realistic scenarios where (a) a maintainer manually invokes a skipped target, (b) stale branches accumulate across many runs, (c) the cron and manual paths diverge mid-skip-window. A reviewer running `/optimize` for the second consecutive month on a real project would hit at least one of these undocumented interactions.
findings.proposed_change: Extend R13 with an explicit manual-override clause: 'Manual invocation of `/optimize {target}` on a target in the 30-day-skip state proceeds with the chat-line warning surfaced (not refused). On manual invocation that lands a `merged` decision (the human accepted the variant), the 30-day skip is cleared — the cron resumes targeting the skill on its next nightly run. On manual invocation that lands `closed-without-merge`, the skip window is NOT extended (the prior streak\'s skip continues to expire on its original schedule).' Add a non-goal note for stale-branch accumulation: 'Stale-branch housekeeping is out of scope for `/optimize` v1 — the branch retention contract (≥30 days) is the lower bound; the upper bound is left to a separate housekeeping skill (deferred). Maintainers running `/optimize` long-term may need to manually prune `optimize/*` branches periodically.' Add an AC verifying the manual-override clause: 'AC-X. With a target in the 30-day-skip state, manual invocation of `/optimize {target}` proceeds AND the chat-line warning is surfaced before pre-flight. A subsequent `merged` decision clears the skip; a subsequent `closed-without-merge` decision does not extend the skip.' This documents the interactions the binary present/absent framing missed.
